thesis: Chime fell about 4.0% to $32.93 (from $34.29) on 8.9x volume (about 40.3M shares against a 4.5M 30-day average). This run found no company disclosure, offering, block trade or lock-up expiry for today, so the driver of the heavy selling is unidentified. The holder-selling record continues: a Nov 17 MarketBeat filing alert says insiders sold 15.04M shares worth about $495.6M over the last quarter and Aspect Management cut its stake 20.9% in Q3; a Crosslink affiliate filed a Form 144 around Nov 13 to sell 36,000 shares; and co-founder Ryan King sold 63,382 shares on Nov 5 under a 10b5-1 plan. The litigation check found consumer data-breach class actions over an April 2026 incident (Castaneda v. Chime, N.D. Cal. 3:26-cv-02924, and Walsh v. Chime), with no scheduled ruling found, no securities class action and no restatement; a reported CFPB refund-delay penalty appears only on a secondary site and was not verified. An unexplained high-volume drop under continuing holder supply makes the evidence mixed; low, avoid.
invalidation: The selling is explained by a one-off holder sale that clears, and a company-disclosed result drives the shares again.
sources: MarketBeat (Aspect stake cut, insider sales last quarter): https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/filing-chime-financial-inc-chym-shares-sold-by-aspect-management-llc-2026-11-17/

thesis: BILL Holdings rose about 12.7% to $64.97 (from $57.63) on 6.7x volume, about 0.7% below its 52-week high, after a Financial Times report that TPG is leading a consortium in talks to acquire the company at a premium to its roughly $4.8B value. The report says timing could change or the talks could fall apart, and no deal has been announced. Truist, William Blair and Morgan Stanley took more constructive stances the same day. Background: Starboard (8.5% stake, 2025) and Elliott (at least 5%) have pressed the company, and Bloomberg reported in 2025 that it was soliciting interest from rivals and private equity. The litigation check found no securities class action, investigation or restatement. A move driven by an unconfirmed takeover report is rumor-driven; low, avoid.
invalidation: A definitive agreement is announced (the stock then trades to the deal price), or the talks end and a company-disclosed result drives the shares.
sources: Benzinga (52-week high as TPG eyes buyout): https://www.benzinga.com/m-a/26/11/63363303/bill-holdings-hits-52-week-high-as-tpg-eyes-buyout

thesis: Bright Horizon Energy (formerly Black Hills) fell about 5.3% to $80.87 (from $85.42) on 4.5x volume in its second session under the HZN ticker; this run found no company news dated today. The all-stock merger with NorthWestern Energy closed on Nov 13 (0.98 HZN shares per NorthWestern share) and the combined company began trading on Nov 16, so the volume and the 60-day move reflect merger mechanics and holder turnover rather than an operating result. Opponents have also gone to court asking a judge to void the Montana PSC's 3-2 approval order 'to the extent it authorizes merger consummation'; NorthWestern does not comment on pending litigation and no hearing date was found. A merger-driven, mechanical move with an open legal challenge makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: Post-merger trading settles and the first combined-company guidance or results drive the shares, with the Montana challenge dismissed.

thesis: Thomson Reuters fell about 3.9% to $104.11 (from $108.29) on 3.3x volume, about 27% below its 52-week high; this run found no company news dated today. The most recent company results were negative: on Nov 3 the stock fell about 9.9% after Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.81 missed the $0.89 estimate, and it fell a further 3.8% on Nov 9 on continued selling. The company announced a $500M buyback around Nov 11 amid AI-spending fears, which has not held the shares. The litigation check found a favorable outcome: on Sep 29, 2026 the Third Circuit affirmed that Ross Intelligence's use of Westlaw headnotes was not fair use; no investigation or restatement found. With the 60-day gain measured from a lower base and no identified positive catalyst for today's move, the evidence is mixed; low, avoid.
invalidation: A company-disclosed result or guidance shows AI products offsetting the Q3 miss, and the shares recover above the pre-miss level.

thesis: TXNM Energy was flat at $58.935 (from $58.94), about 1.0% below its 52-week high, trading as a deal-bound stock under Blackstone's pending $11.5B buyout. The New Mexico PRC voted 2-1 with its hearing examiners that the related $400M stock sale to Blackstone affiliates violated state law because PRC approval was not sought first; the commission stopped short of denying the merger, but the application's timeline will likely be pushed back while the PRC checks compliance. The NRC and FERC are also reviewing the deal, and this run found no November hearing date. The near-high signal reflects deal-bound trading, so the move is mechanical; low, avoid.
invalidation: The merger is terminated or its terms change, so the stock trades on fundamentals again.

thesis: Con Edison fell about 2.1% to $119.31 (from $121.88) on 3.1x volume, about 2.8% below its 52-week high, after announcing on Nov 16 a 6M-share common stock offering under a forward sale agreement with BofA Securities. Proceeds arrive when the forward settles (expected by Dec 31, 2027) and go to subsidiary capital needs; the offering adds to a $2B at-the-market equity program launched in May 2026. The shares also go ex-dividend ($0.887) on Nov 18. The litigation check found the PSC's Jan 22, 2026 three-year rate order (about 87% below the original request), a post-trial motion in an employment case (Burke) and a manhole-death suit, with no scheduled ruling found within 90 days and no restatement. An offering-driven, mechanical move makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The forward offering is absorbed and a company-disclosed result or rate decision drives the shares.

thesis: AECOM rose about 11.1% to $80.56 (from $72.50) on 3.2x volume after its fiscal Q4 2026 report (8-K release dated Nov 16, after the close): adjusted EPS rose 20% to $1.63, above the $1.58 estimate; the adjusted EBITDA margin reached a quarterly record of 19.2% (up 170bp); backlog hit a record of about $28B; the quarterly dividend was raised 10%; and coverage says fiscal 2027 EBITDA guidance tops consensus. Counter-cases remain open: Q4 revenue fell 7.1% to $3.88B on a construction-management slowdown, full-year GAAP EPS from continuing operations fell 41% to $2.84 on a $337M pretax charge for a delayed construction-management project, and the balance-sheet claims that drove the May drop (about $680M, up from about $400M) were not shown to be resolved. The litigation check found Pomerantz and Howard G. Smith investigation notices since June 2026 (solicitations, latest Sep 2) tied to those claims and the charge, with no filed complaint or scheduled step found; no restatement. The shares remain about 40% below their 52-week high. A confirmed beat with record margins and backlog, and the construction-management counter-case unresolved, makes this medium.
invalidation: Construction-management claims or charges grow, fiscal 2027 guidance is cut, a securities complaint is filed, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$72.50).
sources: Trader's Agency (revenue decline, FY2027 EBITDA guide): https://tradersagency.com/blog/aecom-revenue-falls-7percent-in-q4-fy2026-on-construction-management-drag-eps-beats-and-backlog-hits-record-as-fy2027-ebitda-guidance-tops-consensus

thesis: Viking rose about 4.4% to $94.29 (from $90.28) on 2.5x volume after its Q3 2026 report (company release, Nov 17), which missed on both lines: revenue rose 9.2% to $2.18B but came in below estimates, adjusted EPS of $1.11 missed estimates of $1.26-1.28, net income was $498.4M (from $514.0M) and adjusted EBITDA fell 4.3% to $673.5M. Low European river water cost about $100M of revenue and margin, affected about 70% of river capacity, and cut occupancy to 91.3% from 96.0%. The positives are forward-looking: 68% of 2027 capacity is already sold (this run found no prior-year comparison) and $350M was returned through buybacks in the quarter. The litigation check found no 2026 lawsuit, investigation or restatement. A miss with the rebound resting on a bookings figure this run could not benchmark makes the evidence mixed; low, avoid.
invalidation: A company disclosure shows 2027 bookings ahead of the prior year and river disruptions do not recur, so the miss proves one-off.
sources: Investing.com (Q3 slides, water woes and bookings): https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/viking-q3-2026-slides-water-woes-dent-margins-bookings-stay-strong-93CH-5033256

thesis: H World fell about 2.3% to $53.61 (from $54.88) on 2.4x volume, giving back part of Monday's gain, and sits about 5.3% below its 52-week high and still above the ~$50.39 pre-report close. The company-specific catalyst is its Nov 16 Q3 2026 report (6-K): full-year group revenue growth guidance was raised to 9-10% from 4-8%, China segment (HWC) growth guidance to 13-14% from 7-11%, and manachised-and-franchised revenue growth guidance to 22-23% from 16-20%; RTTNews reports Q3 profit climbed, and the company has a three-year shareholder return plan of up to $2.5B approved in August. Counter-cases remain open: the release cites a segment revenue decline of 7.7% to RMB1.2B (the search snippet did not name the segment), today's pullback came without new company news, and analysts had cut ratings to Hold after a Q2 EPS miss ($0.70 vs $0.74). The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. A confirmed guidance raise with the segment decline unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: The raised guidance is cut, the declining segment keeps shrinking, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$50.39).

thesis: Waste Connections fell about 8.1% to $181.41 (from $197.30) on 2.5x volume after a methane gas eruption at its Chiquita Canyon Landfill in Los Angeles County; Seeking Alpha reports the shares closed down 8%, TokenPost reports a roughly 500-foot geyser of trash and six people hospitalized, and Finimize says the leak was capped Monday night with remediation, monitoring, regulatory and legal costs still unknown. The site already carries heavy litigation: California's Attorney General and DTSC sued the owners and operators on Oct 27, 2026; Los Angeles County has a federal suit over the elevated-temperature event; EPA required more work under its unilateral order in March 2026; and a trial date of April 23 is reported with the year unclear. A new adverse incident with unquantified liability makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The company quantifies the Chiquita Canyon cost and regulators accept a remediation plan, so an operating result drives the shares again.
sources: Seeking Alpha (shares plunge after methane eruption): https://seekingalpha.com/news/4673927-waste-connections-plunges-after-methane-gas-eruption-at-los-angeles-area-landfill

thesis: Freshworks fell about 2.1% to $12.955 (from $13.23) on 3.3x volume. A Betaville report said the company may have attracted takeover interest from an undisclosed buyer; Freshworks declined to comment on the rumor and confirmed to Bloomberg it is no longer participating in a UBS conference next week. Earlier in November, UBS raised its target to $17 from $14 after the company's report. The litigation check found only the 2021-22 IPO securities class action (lead-plaintiff deadlines in January 2022) and no 2026 lawsuit, investigation or restatement. A move tied to an unconfirmed takeover rumor is rumor-driven; low, avoid.
invalidation: A buyer or a definitive agreement is confirmed, or the rumor fades and a company-disclosed result drives the shares.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). thesis: Held position (opened Nov 12 on the Nov 11 proposal).
